page.overview:
Who is Shigeru Miyamoto?

Shigeru Miyamoto is a Japanese video game designer, artist and producer, and the creator of .

During his childhood, Miyamoto enjoyed exploring the countryside and hillsides around his home, which inspired the creation of The Legend of Zelda franchise. He joined Nintendo in 1977, where he began developing early arcade games such as Sheriff and Donkey Kong (his first major hit), and through his long and highly successful professional career, would become one of the most accomplished and influential video game designers in the world and is primarily responsible for making the company widely known as it is today (Nintendo before Miyamoto's employment was a small Japanese card/toy manufacturer). Shortly before starting development for Super Mario Bros., Miyamoto began developing The Legend of Zelda as a launch title for the Famicom Disk System (an add-on for the Japanese version of the NES). Since then, he has worked as the producer of every game in the Zelda series. He is also the creator of other iconic Nintendo franchises such as Mario, [https://donkeykong.fandom.com/wiki/Donkey_Kong_(series) Donkey Kong], F-Zero, Star Fox, and Pikmin, as well as [https://nintendogs.fandom.com/wiki/Main_Page Nintendogs], and played important roles in the creation of Metroid and Pokémon. In 2002, Shigeru Miyamoto served as one of Nintendo's representative directors as an executive and was promoted to the title of Fellow at Nintendo in 2015. He continues to work at Nintendo to this day.

Also known as: Miyamoto.
